entry.title: Prevent unintended Amazon RDS cluster replacement when Terraform reads a dynamic Availability Zone list
entry.content: AWS Regions grow over time as new Availability Zones are added. If your Terraform configuration reads the Region’s Availability Zone list dynamically and passes it directly into a database resource, that growth can have an unexpected consequence: the next terraform apply can propose deleting and rebuilding your cluster. In this post, you learn why this happens, how to prevent it in your Terraform, and how to protect the data on independent layers even if a destructive change slips through.

entry.title: Reduce storage costs by migrating over-provisioned io2 volumes to gp3
entry.content: Many workloads still run Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) EBS volumes chosen years ago, before gp3 existed. Because io2 bills for every provisioned IOPS on top of storage, a volume provisioned far above its real usage adds unnecessary cost every month. This article shows how to identify over-provisioned io2 volumes and migrate them to gp3 with no downtime on current-generation instances.

entry.title: When the first Data API statement to an idle Amazon Redshift Serverless workgroup fails: using RedshiftQueryId to tell whether the SQL ran
entry.content: The first Data API statement sent to an idle Amazon Redshift Serverless workgroup can fail with an internal error, while resending the same SQL as a new statement succeeds. entry.title: Restarting an Amazon MSK Connect connector: what it covers and how to measure how long it takes
entry.content: n MSK Connect restart preserves all configuration and committed offsets, runs asynchronously, and requires the connector to be RUNNING with no other lifecycle operation in progress. This article covers what a restart does and does not cover, how behavior differs between Apache Kafka Connect 3.7 and 2.7.1, why RESTART_COMPLETE does not mean the tasks are healthy, why update and delete are blocked during a restart, and how to measure the actual duration with creationTime and endTime.

entry.title: Investigating repeated Kafka Streams rebalances on Amazon MSK when no member joined or left (probing rebalances)
entry.content: On Amazon MSK, a Kafka Streams application can rebalance at a regular interval even though no instance joined or left. These are usually probing rebalances. This article covers where to get the client and broker logs on MSK, the log lines that confirm it, the defaults and lower bounds of probing.rebalance.interval.ms, acceptable.recovery.lag and max.warmup.replicas, why two of them must change together, and why the RebalanceInProgress metric does not answer this question.

entry.title: Why transaction.timeout.ms shows 10000 instead of 60000 in a Kafka Streams EOS application
entry.content: With processing.guarantee=exactly_once_v2, Kafka Streams overrides the producer transaction.timeout.ms to 10,000 ms (not the documented 60,000 ms) and commit.interval.ms to 100 ms. This article shows which values actually apply, why Streams changes them, how to confirm the effective values from the startup log, and the two constraints when you override them: startup fails if transaction.timeout.ms is below commit.interval.ms, and the broker's transaction.max.timeout.ms is the upper bound.
